issue_context.title: File.OpenHandle does not respect FileOptions.DeleteOnClose on Unix
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-io See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Repro: ```C# using System; using System.IO; using Microsoft.Win32.SafeHandles; string path = "test.dat"; var h = File.OpenHandle("test.dat", FileMode.Create, FileAccess.ReadWrite, FileShare.None, FileOptions.DeleteOnClose); Console.WriteLine(File.Exists(path)); h.Dispose(); Console.WriteLine(File.Exists(path)); ``` This should print `true` then `false`, but on Unix it prints `true` then `true`. Note this isn't a case of DeleteOnClose not working on Unix. It does, e.g. change the repro to use: ```C# var h = File.Create("test.dat", 1, FileOptions.DeleteOnClose); ``` instead, and it'll correctly print out the expected results. Rather, the code on Unix to handle emulating FileOptions.DeleteOnClose is part of FileStream.Dispose and should likely instead be a part of SafeFileHandle. cc: @adamsitnik
